retainageCap.notes: Section last amended in 2015 (Statutes of Nevada 2015, p. 2626). The 5% figure was read in current text; the secondary-source claim that 2015 lowered it from 10% and the contract-date applicability of that change were not verified, so appliesFrom is null.

retainageRelease.trigger: No retainage-specific release deadline found in NRS 624.624; the general rule (scheduled due date or 10 days after the higher-tiered contractor receives payment for the work, whichever is earlier) would govern retention received from the owner
retainageRelease.notes: Null because the statute text reviewed does not state when retention must be released to a lower-tiered subcontractor. Applying the 10-day rule to retention is an inference. Owner-side sections (NRS 624.609-624.622) were not read in full.

payIfPaid.cite: APCO Constr., Inc. v. Zitting Bros. Constr., Inc., 136 Nev. 569, 473 P.3d 1021 (2020); NRS 624.628(3); Lehrer McGovern Bovis, Inc. v. Bullock Insulation, Inc., 124 Nev. 1102, 197 P.3d 1032 (2008)
payIfPaid.notes: Treat as effectively void in practice. Lehrer (2008) said pay-if-paid provisions are generally unenforceable as against public policy; APCO v. Zitting (2020) clarified they are not per se void but are unenforceable whenever they require a sub to waive or limit rights under NRS 624.624-624.630 or relieve the GC of its obligations under those sections (NRS 624.628(3)), and held the clause there void because it limited the right to prompt payment; Helix Elec. v. APCO (Nev. 2022) reached the same result. Commentators say enforceable only in extremely limited circumstances. Classified 'limited' because the Nevada Supreme Court expressly rejected a per se rule; a conservative system should not rely on pay-if-paid in Nevada. Opinions known through summaries, not read in full; reporter citation for Lehrer is from memory of the standard citation and should be verified.

lienWaiver.notes: Stricter than 'substantially': a waiver or release is 'unenforceable unless it is in the following forms'. Any contract term that attempts to waive or impair lien rights is void (108.2453(2), 108.2457(1)); a waiver is enforceable only if the claimant signs the statutory form and, for conditional waivers, receives the payment. NRS 108.2457(5)(e): a waiver is void if the payment check fails to clear. No notary block in the forms.

promptPay.lateInterest: 1% per month (or fraction of a month) on the unpaid balance, or a higher contract rate, 'notwithstanding any contrary agreement'
promptPay.notes: Seven days after receipt of good funds for each interim or final payment, provided contractually required documentation and waivers are received. The 7 days is high-confidence (statute read). Override is the uncertain part: § 756-a says contract terms supersede the article 'except as otherwise provided', but § 757(4) voids payment provisions differing from § 756-a(3), so set to false. Applies only to private contracts with total cost >= $150,000; excludes 1-3 family dwellings, certain residential tracts and small/affordable residential projects (§ 756).

retainageCap.conditions: Private construction contracts >= $150,000 (GBL § 756 definition). 5% of the contract sum; a GC/sub may not retain from a sub more than the actual percentage retained by the owner.
retainageCap.notes: Cap added by L.2023 (S3539/A4167), effective for contracts entered on/after 2023-11-17. RECENT AMENDMENT: SB 5655 signed 2025-12-19, effective immediately, added § 757(5) making any provision requiring retainage above 5% of the contract sum void (closing the contract-around loophole). Cap and § 757(5) read on nysenate.gov; dates from law-firm alerts (Holland & Knight, Venable, Cozen).

retainageRelease.trigger: after final approval of the work (owner must release retainage to the contractor; same section imposes 1%/month interest on an owner, contractor or subcontractor that fails to release retainage as required)
retainageRelease.notes: The 30-day rule is written as owner-to-contractor; the statute gives no separate number of days for GC-to-sub retainage. The 7-day pass-through of § 756-a(3)(b)(ii) applies to final payment funds received.

payIfPaid.cite: West-Fair Elec. Contractors v. Aetna Cas. & Sur. Co., 87 N.Y.2d 148 (1995) (construing Lien Law § 34)
payIfPaid.notes: Clauses shifting the risk of owner nonpayment to the sub are void as against public policy; pay-when-paid clauses that only fix a reasonable time for payment are allowed. A choice of another state's law could avoid the rule (Welsbach Elec. v. MasTec, 7 N.Y.3d 624 (2006)), but GBL § 757(1) voids out-of-state choice of law in covered contracts. Holding taken from search summaries of the opinion.

lienWaiver.notes: Statute read: contractual waiver of the right to file or enforce a lien is void as against public policy; waivers executed simultaneously with or after payment are permitted. No statutory form or notarization requirement (secondary source: Siteline 50-state survey).

promptPay.lateInterest: 18% per annum on the payment due, beginning on the eleventh day after the contractor receives payment from the owner
promptPay.notes: 10 CALENDAR days after receipt of payment from the owner, when the sub's pay request was submitted in time to be included in the GC's own pay request. Override false: under (D)(2) the statute prevails over contract terms with longer periods or lower interest, and (D)(1) voids waiver of interest/fees; a shorter contractual period is fine. Version in force is effective 2011-09-29. PENDING: H.B. 288 (136th G.A.) would add an owner-to-GC 30-day duty; reported by House committee but not passed as of this research; predecessor H.B. 203 died in the Senate.

retainageCap.conditions: No statutory cap on private work; § 4113.61(A)(1) allows the GC to reduce payment 'by any retainage provision contained in the contract'.
retainageCap.notes: Absence of a private cap confirmed only by secondary source (Levelset); public-works retainage rules in R.C. ch. 153 do not apply.

retainageRelease.trigger: after GC receives retainage from the owner (calendar days, or any shorter contract period), for subs whose work the owner has approved
retainageRelease.notes: 18% per annum interest applies to late retainage as well.

payIfPaid.cite: Transtar Elec., Inc. v. A.E.M. Elec. Servs. Corp., 140 Ohio St.3d 193, 2014-Ohio-3095; Ohio Rev. Code § 4113.62(E)
payIfPaid.notes: Ohio Supreme Court enforces clear pay-if-paid clauses ('condition precedent' wording suffices). By statute, a contingent-payment clause cannot bar the sub from filing a lien or bond claim to keep those rights from expiring while payment is pending. Case holding from Court News Ohio/law-firm summaries; § 4113.62(E) read on codes.ohio.gov. Reporter cite 140 Ohio St.3d 193 is from memory, not verified.

lienWaiver.cite: No statute (R.C. ch. 1311 silent on waiver form); see § 4113.62(E)
lienWaiver.notes: Single secondary source (Levelset): no statutory forms, no notarization requirement, advance waivers not prohibited (though disfavored). Exception: a contract with a pay-if-paid clause cannot prevent lien filing (§ 4113.62(E), read).

promptPay.notes: Statute text as reproduced by Levelset: 'Subcontractors shall be paid by the prime contractor within ten (10) calendar days of payment from the owner, or as otherwise agreed to by the parties.' Husch Blackwell agrees (10 days, unless otherwise agreed). I could not open the official text (Justia 403, OSCN lookup failed), so the exact subsection letter is unverified; one outlier source (LegalFix) says 7 days. lateInterest null: Levelset FAQ and Husch Blackwell say no statutory interest on private projects, though another Levelset page says 1.5%/month; unresolved. Remedy is suspension of work after 10 days' written notice. Act does not apply to 1-4 family dwellings (§ 821). NOTE: the 'Fair Pay for Construction Act' (61 O.S. §§ 221-227: 5% retainage, 7/10-day rules) is PUBLIC works only.

retainageCap.conditions: No statutory cap on private work; § 820 lets payments be reduced by retainage as provided in the contract/subcontract.
retainageCap.cite: No private statute (61 O.S. § 226's 5% cap is public-only)
retainageCap.notes: Confirmed 61 O.S. § 226 is titled public construction by reading enrolled H.B. 1114 (2019). Absence of a private cap per Levelset.

retainageRelease.notes: Null: no private retainage release statute. The default 10-day pass-through of 15 O.S. § 820 would apply to funds received absent contrary agreement.

payIfPaid.cite: Swanda Bros., Inc. v. Chasco Constructors, Ltd. (W.D. Okla., No. 5:08-cv-00199) (applying Oklahoma law)
payIfPaid.notes: Federal courts applying Oklahoma law have enforced clear condition-precedent clauses and noted no Oklahoma statute prohibits them, but there is no Oklahoma appellate decision on point. Opinion not read directly; I did not confirm the full list of void provisions in 15 O.S. § 821.

lienWaiver.notes: Single secondary source (Levelset): no statutory forms, no notarization requirement, statutes silent on advance waivers and courts have not definitively ruled.

promptPay.lateInterest: 1.5% per month (or fraction of a month) on the unpaid balance, or a higher agreed rate, beginning on the eighth day
promptPay.notes: Seven calendar days after the original contractor receives payment from the owner. The 7 days and interest are read from the 2025 ORS edition. Override false at medium confidence: ORS 701.630 has no opt-out and ORS 701.625(8) bars contract changes that alter a subcontractor's right to prompt payment, but there is no general anti-waiver clause. GC may withhold for listed reasons. ORS 701.620-701.640 do not apply to Low-Rise Residential Dwelling Code buildings, public contracts, or certain income-restricted housing (ORS 701.645).

retainageCap.conditions: Owner, contractor or subcontractor may withhold not more than 5% of the contract price of the work completed. Not applicable where the owner is the United States or federal money pays for the work (ORS 701.440). A surety bond may be posted in lieu of retainage (ORS 701.435).
retainageCap.notes: Read in 2025 ORS edition. Last amended by Or. Laws 2024, ch. 2 (HB 4006), which per secondary sources repealed the 2019 interest-bearing escrow requirement for contracts over $500,000 and expanded the retainage-bond alternative. The page notes some ch. 701 sections were touched in the 2026 session; none seen for these sections, but the 2026 A&R table was not checked.

retainageRelease.trigger: after the contractor/subcontractor has completed and the owner has accepted the work (final payment then accrues 1%/month interest); party notified of completion has 15 days to accept or list remaining work
retainageRelease.notes: This is an interest-accrual trigger, not a pass-through deadline. Separately, ORS 701.630(2)(a) requires the GC to pay subs within 7 days of receiving a progress or final payment from the owner; use 7 days for pass-through of retainage funds actually received.

payIfPaid.cite: No Oregon statute or appellate decision found
payIfPaid.notes: Husch Blackwell (2020) lists pay-if-paid as permissible in Oregon but cites no authority, and I found no Oregon appellate decision; marked unsettled rather than enforceable.

lienWaiver.cite: No statute (ORS ch. 87 has no waiver form); ORS 701.630(2)(b)
lienWaiver.notes: Single secondary source (Levelset): no statutory forms; advance waivers not prohibited. Notarization is not required by law, but ORS 701.630(2)(b) lets a GC or sub require notarized lien waivers by contract.

promptPay.lateInterest: 1% per month (or fraction of a month) on the balance due, from the day after the due date; plus a 1% per month penalty on amounts wrongfully withheld and attorney fees if arbitration/litigation is brought
promptPay.notes: 14 days after receipt of each progress or final payment OR 14 days after receipt of the sub's invoice, whichever is later. Override false: § 7(c) has no agree-otherwise language and § 3(c) (added by Act 27 of 2018) bars waiver of the act by contract. If the GC fails to disclose the owner's payment due date before the subcontract is signed, it must pay as though the owner paid on time (§ 7(b)). Act does not apply to six or fewer residential units under construction simultaneously. Read in the official consolidated act; 73 P.S. section numbers are the conventional Purdon's mapping of Act sections.

retainageCap.conditions: No statutory cap on private work. A sub may post a maintenance bond for 120% of retainage at substantial completion of its scope to obtain early release (§ 9(a.1)).
retainageCap.notes: Full text of the act read; it regulates timing only, not percentage.

retainageRelease.trigger: after GC receives the retainage from the owner (owner must release within 30 days after final acceptance of the work; if the owner holds no retainage, GC must pay sub retainage within 30 days after final acceptance)
retainageRelease.notes: Late retainage accrues 1%/month interest plus § 12 penalty exposure.

payIfPaid.cite: Sloan & Co. v. Liberty Mut. Ins. Co., 653 F.3d 175 (3d Cir. 2011)
payIfPaid.notes: Third Circuit (predicting Pennsylvania law) enforces clearly worded pay-if-paid clauses; a Philadelphia trial court followed it (Pencoyd Iron Works). No Pennsylvania Supreme Court decision. Open questions: an E.D. Pa. 2018 decision (Connelly) recognized an exception where the GC caused nonpayment, and whether the 2018 CASPA anti-waiver provision (§ 3(c)) affects such clauses is unresolved.

lienWaiver.cite: 49 P.S. § 1401 (Mechanics' Lien Law of 1963 § 401, as amended by Act 52 of 2006)
lienWaiver.notes: Since 2007-01-01 advance lien waivers on non-residential projects are against public policy and void except to the extent payment is actually received. Exceptions: residential projects (contract price under $1,000,000), and subcontractor waivers where the contractor has posted a payment bond. Statute text not read directly; based on consistent law-firm summaries. No statutory form or notarization requirement (Siteline survey).

promptPay.cite: No private prompt-pay statute (R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 42-11.1 covers state-funded work only)
promptPay.notes: Null because Rhode Island does not regulate GC-to-sub payment timing on private projects, per Husch Blackwell, Levelset and a Practical Law/Pierce Atwood guide. One outlier (LegalFix) claims a 10-day private rule under § 37-13, which is the public-works wage chapter; disregarded. P.L. 2024 ch. 229 shortened the sub-payment period to 7 days for STATE contracts only (§ 42-11.1-3(b)). No 2024-2026 private prompt-pay enactment found.

retainageCap.conditions: 5% of any progress payment. Applies only to a 'contract for construction' under § 5-65-1: lienable (private) or public projects with an original contract price of at least $250,000; excludes projects of one to four dwelling units. After substantial completion, withholding is further limited (150% of cost to complete/correct, 2.5% for missing deliverables, 0.5% for first-year defects).
retainageCap.notes: Read on the General Assembly site. Although codified in the public-works bond chapter, it expressly covers private lienable contracts via § 5-65-1. Enacted by P.L. 2018, ch. 170; exact effective date/contract-date applicability not confirmed, so appliesFrom left null. Levelset's summary table wrongly shows 'not regulated'.

retainageRelease.trigger: after submission of an application for payment of retainage, which may be submitted once 60 days have passed after substantial completion; each lower tier's payment period may be extended 7 days beyond the tier above (so up to 37 days for a first-tier sub)
retainageRelease.notes: Triggered by the retainage application, not by GC's receipt of funds. The exact mechanics of the 7-day tier extension were summarized by the fetch tool, not read verbatim; verify before hard-coding 30 vs 37. Same $250,000 / 1-4 unit limits apply.

payIfPaid.cite: No controlling Rhode Island authority found (issue raised in Petrolex II LLC v. Bailey Group LLC, R.I. 2023, No. 22-10)
payIfPaid.notes: Husch Blackwell: 'Unclear. Rhode Island has not yet addressed contingent payment clauses.' Practical Law says common law does not ban them. In Petrolex II a party argued the clause was void as against public policy; I could not confirm that the court decided the question.

lienWaiver.notes: Statute read: any covenant purporting to bar filing a notice of intention or enforcing a lien is against public policy, void and unenforceable; written waivers executed simultaneously with or after payment are permitted. No statutory form or notarization requirement (Siteline survey).

promptPay.lateInterest: 1% per month
promptPay.notes: Read on the official code page. Contractor (and each sub) must pay its subs within 7 days of receiving a periodic or final payment; owner has 21 days from receipt of pay request. Interest (§ 29-6-50) accrues only if the payee gave notice of § 29-6-50 when requesting payment. Private contracts may set different payment periods/interest rates ONLY if §§ 29-6-30 and 29-6-50 are specifically waived by section number in conspicuous bold-faced or underlined type.

retainageCap.notes: No percentage cap found for private work. § 29-6-40 permits withholding 'a reasonable amount for retainage'. Absence of a cap confirmed against Chapter 6 text only; not an exhaustive search of the code.

retainageRelease.trigger: after GC receives payment (periodic or final) from owner - general prompt-pay rule, not a retainage-specific provision
retainageRelease.notes: No retainage-specific release deadline found. The 7-day pass-through in § 29-6-30 applies to any periodic or final payment received; treating released retainage as such a payment is an inference, hence medium.

payIfPaid.cite: S.C. Code Ann. § 29-6-230
payIfPaid.notes: Statute: payment by the owner to the contractor is not a condition precedent to payment of a subcontractor; 'Any agreement to the contrary is not enforceable.'

lienWaiver.notes: § 29-7-20: an agreement to waive the right to file or claim a lien for labor and materials is against public policy and unenforceable unless payment substantially equal to the amount waived is actually made (statute text seen via search-result excerpt of the official page, not a full read). No statutory form and no notarization requirement per secondary sources (Levelset).

promptPay.notes: No private-project prompt-payment statute found. SDCL ch. 5-26 covers public contracts only. Husch Blackwell (2020) lists private deadlines as N/A; Siteline agrees. One Levelset page claims a 45-day default applies to private work - not corroborated and not adopted here.

retainageCap.notes: No private-project retainage statute per secondary sources; statutory retainage schedule is public-works only.

retainageRelease.notes: No statutory deadline for private projects found.

payIfPaid.notes: No statute or reported South Dakota decision located; Husch Blackwell (2020): 'South Dakota has not yet addressed contingent payment clauses.'

lienWaiver.notes: No fill-in statutory waiver form. Ch. 44-9A provides an optional joint-check waiver method (joint check + separate written waiver agreement + provision on reverse of check); § 44-9A-1 preserves other waiver methods. Only the chapter's section titles were readable on the official site; substance is from a single secondary source (ezel.ai). That source says no statute voids advance waivers, but this was not confirmed against SDCL ch. 44-9 text, so advanceWaiverVoid left null.

promptPay.lateInterest: contract rate if stated; otherwise 1.5% per month from due date
promptPay.notes: days is null because the current statute is NOT keyed to the GC's receipt of owner payment. § 66-34-302(a) (as amended by 2020 Pub. Ch. 749, eff. July 1, 2020 for contracts entered/amended/renewed on or after that date): prime must pay the remote contractor per the contract's payment schedule AND within 30 days after the remote contractor's timely application for payment, 'subject only to any condition precedent for payment clause in the contract' and less amounts withheld under § 66-34-303. Husch Blackwell's 2020 survey states '30 days after prime receives payment from owner' - this conflicts with the statute text read (FindLaw copy current as of Jan 2024; official code is on LexisNexis and was not accessible). Whether the 30-day outer limit can be lengthened by contract is unclear -> null. Act reportedly does not apply to 1-4 unit residential (secondary).

retainageCap.conditions: Applies to all construction contracts on any project in the state, public and private. Separate escrow requirement in § 66-34-104 for certain contracts (threshold not verified here).
retainageCap.notes: Statute text read on FindLaw (current as of Jan 2, 2024): retainage 'may not exceed five percent (5%) of the amount of the contract.' Violation is a Class A misdemeanor, $3,000 fine per day, plus restitution (§ 66-34-103(e)). Medium only because the official LexisNexis-hosted code could not be read directly.

retainageRelease.trigger: after prime contractor receives the retainage from the owner (owner must release within 90 days after completion of the work or substantial completion of the project, whichever first)
retainageRelease.notes: Same 10-day pass-through applies down each tier. Read on FindLaw copy (Jan 2024).

payIfPaid.cite: Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-34-302(a); Koch v. Construction Technology, Inc., 924 S.W.2d 68 (Tenn. 1996)
payIfPaid.notes: § 66-34-302(a) expressly makes the prime's payment duty 'subject only to any condition precedent for payment clause in the contract'. Koch (opinion not read directly; secondary summaries) treated an ordinary pay-when-paid clause as a timing provision, requiring clear, unequivocal condition-precedent language to shift nonpayment risk.

lienWaiver.notes: § 66-11-124(b)(1): a contract provision waiving lien rights 'is void and unenforceable as against the public policy of this state'; contractors who solicit such waivers risk license revocation. No statutory form or notarization requirement appears in the section. FindLaw copy current as of Jan 2024.

promptPay.lateInterest: 1.5% per month, accruing from the day after payment is due
promptPay.notes: Contractor must pay each sub 'not later than the seventh day after the date the contractor receives the owner's payment' (owner has 35 days from receipt of payment request). § 28.006(a): attempted waiver of Chapter 28 is void (only exception: owner-contractor single-family residence contracts). Text read on texas.public.law mirror (verified May 2025); the official statutes.capitol.texas.gov page did not render.

retainageCap.notes: No statutory cap on retainage a GC may withhold from a sub on private work. § 53.101 instead REQUIRES the owner to reserve 10% of the contract price (or value of work) until 30 days after completion ('reserved funds', as amended by HB 2237 eff. Jan 1, 2022) - an owner obligation, not a cap. 2025 session bills touching § 53.101 (SB 2131/HB 3712, SB 1530) were not confirmed enacted.

retainageRelease.trigger: after GC receives payment from owner - general prompt-pay rule, not a retainage-specific provision
retainageRelease.notes: No retainage-specific pass-through statute found; § 28.002(b) 7-day rule covers the portion of any owner payment attributable to the sub's work. Applying it to released retainage is an inference.

payIfPaid.cite: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code §§ 56.052, 56.054
payIfPaid.notes: Contingent payment clauses are enforceable but limited by Ch. 56: (1) § 56.052 - after the 45th day following its payment request the sub may send written objection; once effective, the clause cannot be enforced for work performed afterward; (2) § 56.054 - clause may not be enforced if unconscionable (safe harbor requires GC diligence on owner's financial viability and collection efforts/assignment). Other Ch. 56 sections (e.g., where nonpayment is due to GC's own breach) not read.

lienWaiver.notes: § 53.284(a): waiver unenforceable unless it substantially complies with the applicable form. § 53.281(b): must be signed by claimant; no notarization requirement appears in current text (amended by HB 2237, eff. Jan 1, 2022). § 53.286: any contract purporting to waive lien/claim rights is void as against public policy except as allowed by § 53.282; § 53.282(a)(3) allows pre-work contractual waivers only for single-family house/townhouse/duplex contracts. Unconditional forms require actual payment (§ 53.283, title only read).

promptPay.lateInterest: 1% per month of the amount due, plus reasonable collection costs and attorney fees
promptPay.notes: Contractor must pay subs/suppliers 'within 30 consecutive days after receiving construction funds from the owner or another contractor' or after the last day payment is due under the billing terms, whichever is later; applies 'unless otherwise agreed by contract' and penalties require failure 'without reasonable cause'. Read on FindLaw (le.utah.gov section page did not render); consistent with Husch Blackwell.

retainageCap.conditions: Written NONRESIDENTIAL commercial or industrial construction contracts (private and public; owner-contractor, contractor-sub, sub-sub). Max 5% of each payment and 5% of total construction price. Mixed-use: applies to nonresidential share by square footage. Owner may withhold more to cure default, or up to 2x fair market value of unfinished work after substantial completion. Cannot be waived.
retainageCap.notes: Read on official le.utah.gov version effective 2/27/2023 (2023 ch. 16). IMPORTANT: that page is marked 'superseded 1/1/2027' - an amended version takes effect Jan 1, 2027; I could not locate the amending bill or the new text, so re-check before 2027.

retainageRelease.trigger: from the day all or any portion of the retention proceeds is received by the contractor (owner must release within 45 days after the latest of: billing statement, certificate of occupancy/final acceptance, permitted occupancy, or acceptance of final pay quantities)
retainageRelease.notes: Knowing and wrongful withholding of retention: 2% per month charge plus attorney fees. Version superseded 1/1/2027 - see retainageCap note.

payIfPaid.cite: Utah Code § 13-8-4(3)
payIfPaid.notes: § 13-8-4 recognizes 'contingent payment contracts' but provides that one 'is not a defense to a claim to enforce a preconstruction or construction lien' (exception: private residential work of 4 units or fewer); sub may request project-financing information before signing. No reported Utah state appellate decision squarely enforcing pay-if-paid was found; commentators (Parr Brown) predict enforcement if clearly drafted, citing Zions First Nat'l Bank v. Christiansen Bros., 66 F.3d 1560 (10th Cir. 1995). So enforceability outside the lien context is probable but not settled.

lienWaiver.notes: Forms are a safe harbor, not mandatory: a waiver 'meets the requirements of this section if it is in substantially the form provided' - conditional progress form at § 38-1a-802(4)(b), final payment form at § 38-1a-802(4)(c), restrictive check endorsement at (4)(d). But ANY waiver is enforceable only if the claimant signs a waiver/release (or restrictive endorsement) AND receives the payment; void if the check fails. § 38-1a-105: contract provisions waiving/limiting lien rights are void except in consideration of payment under § 38-1a-802. No notarization in the forms. Read on FindLaw (current as of Jan 1, 2025).

promptPay.lateInterest: interest penalties 'consistent with § 2.2-4355': prime rate (WSJ base rate on corporate loans) unless the contract provides a different rate, accruing 7 days after payment date
promptPay.notes: GC must pay sub within the EARLIER of (i) 60 days of receipt of the sub's invoice or (ii) seven days after receipt of amounts paid by the owner for that work. Withholding requires written notice (reason, amount) - summarized by the reader as within 50 days. 'Any provision in a contract contrary to this section shall be unenforceable.' Private prompt-pay provisions date from 2022 (cc. 726, 727), amended 2023 (cc. 675, 676). The section may contain project-type/size limits for some provisions (fetch summary mentioned non-single-family projects over $500,000 for flow-down and wage liability) - check full text. 2026 c. 1040 (HB 238) amended the section's wage-liability provisions (GC jointly liable for sub's employees' wages on contracts entered on/after July 1, 2026); it did not appear to change the payment deadlines.

retainageCap.notes: No private cap: § 11-4.6 says its payment provisions do not 'prohibit the inclusion of any retainage provisions in a construction contract.' The 5% cap in § 2.2-4333 is public-works only. NEW 2026: SB 165 (2026 Acts c. 485, approved Apr 8, 2026) adds § 11-4.7 allowing a contractor/sub to tender a retainage bond in lieu of retainage on owner-GC and GC-sub contracts; text and effective date not read (presumably July 1, 2026) - medium/low on that detail.

retainageRelease.trigger: after GC receives payment from owner for the sub's work (or 60 days after the sub's invoice, if earlier) - general prompt-pay rule, not a retainage-specific provision
retainageRelease.notes: No retainage-specific release deadline; applying the general 7-day rule to released retainage is an inference.

payIfPaid.notes: 'Payment by the party contracting with the contractor shall not be a condition precedent to payment to any subcontractor' - exception: 'unless the party contracting with the contractor is insolvent or a debtor in bankruptcy as defined in § 50-73.79.' Contrary provisions unenforceable. Applies to contracts under the 2022/2023 amendments (older contracts may be governed by prior law).

lienWaiver.notes: Lien rights may be waived at any time, EXCEPT a general contractor, subcontractor, lower-tier subcontractor, or material supplier 'may not waive or diminish his lien rights in a contract in advance of furnishing any labor, services, or materials'; such a provision 'is null and void'. No statutory form or notarization requirement in the subsection.

promptPay.lateInterest: interest at the rate set by 12 V.S.A. § 2903(b) from the day after the due date; plus penalty of 1% per month on amounts wrongfully withheld (9 V.S.A. § 4007(b))
promptPay.notes: 'Notwithstanding any contrary agreement', contractor must pay sub 7 days after receipt of each progress or final payment or 7 days after receipt of the sub's invoice, whichever is later. The numeric rate in 12 V.S.A. § 2903(b) was not read (commonly cited as 12% per year - unverified here). Contractor must also disclose owner's payment due dates to subs (§ 4003(b)). § 4008: federal-aid contracts may vary the chapter.

retainageCap.conditions: No retainage may be held on materials delivered by a materialman and accepted by the contractor that carry a manufacturer's warranty and/or meet industry grading standards (9 V.S.A. § 4005(e)).
retainageCap.notes: § 4005 regulates timing but states no percentage cap. Section amended by 2017, No. 179 (Adj. Sess.), § 3.

retainageRelease.trigger: after contractor receives the retainage (owner must pay retainage within 30 days after final acceptance of the work)
retainageRelease.notes: 'Notwithstanding any contrary agreement.' If the owner is not withholding retainage, retainage the contractor holds from a sub is due within 30 days after final acceptance (§ 4005(b)).

payIfPaid.notes: No Vermont statute or appellate decision squarely addressing pay-if-paid was found (Husch Blackwell 2020: 'Unclear'). § 4003(a) entitles a performing sub to payment from the party it contracts with, and § 4003(b) makes a contractor that fails to disclose the owner's due dates pay as if the owner had paid on time, which may undercut such clauses, but no court ruling confirmed.

lienWaiver.notes: No statutory lien waiver form or advance-waiver provision located for Vermont (9 V.S.A. ch. 51 lien statutes not read); searches returned nothing on point. Treat as 'no mandated form' with low confidence; notarization and advance-waiver validity unconfirmed.

promptPay.notes: No private-project prompt-payment statute setting a GC-to-sub deadline found (Husch Blackwell 2020: N/A; RCW 39.76/39.04.250 are public). RCW 60.30.010 (2023) only addresses retainage and interest on final payment.

retainageCap.conditions: Private construction projects only (RCW 60.30.030). Does not apply to single-family residential construction of fewer than 12 units. Applies to owners, contractors, subcontractors and (since June 6, 2024) suppliers. Party may tender a retainage bond in lieu (RCW 60.30.020).
retainageCap.notes: 'not more than five percent of the contract price of the work completed.' Enacted by Laws 2023 c 373 (SSB 5528), effective July 23, 2023; the act contains no clause limiting it to contracts entered after that date, so appliesFrom is null (statute simply effective 2023-07-23). Amended by Laws 2024 c 101 (SSB 6108), effective June 6, 2024, adding suppliers.

retainageRelease.trigger: No hard deadline. Interest at 1% per month on the final payment starts 30 days after work is completed and accepted (or 30 days after a 15-day response window following notice of completion lapses). A contractor's interest obligation to a sub does not begin until the contractor has been paid that retainage, provided it submitted the request upstream within 30 days of receiving it.
retainageRelease.notes: Statute sets when interest begins rather than a fixed pass-through deadline; days left null. On posting of a retainage bond, withheld funds must be released within 30 days (RCW 60.30.020).

payIfPaid.cite: Amelco Electric v. Donald M. Drake Co., 20 Wn. App. 899 (1978) (pay-when-paid construed as timing only)
payIfPaid.notes: No statute; no controlling published decision squarely enforcing or voiding a true pay-if-paid clause was confirmed. Secondary sources split: Husch Blackwell (2020) lists pay-if-paid as permissible; others say unclear. Amelco citation reporter details are from memory of secondary sources and were not verified against the opinion. A 2024 Div. II opinion (Pease & Sons v. Turner Constr., No. 58748-3-II, apparently unpublished) discussed such clauses but could not be read.

lienWaiver.notes: No statutory waiver form in ch. 60.04 RCW per secondary sources. Ch. 60.04 has no express ban on advance/prospective waivers and commentary (Stoel Rives, Levelset) says common law permits them, so advanceWaiverVoid=false at low confidence - statute text not read. Notarization not confirmed either way.

promptPay.notes: No private-project prompt-payment statute setting a GC-to-sub deadline found (Husch Blackwell 2020: N/A). Wis. Stat. § 779.135(3) allows clauses that delay payment until the prime is paid (pay-when-paid) but not ones making it a condition precedent.

retainageCap.notes: No private-project retainage cap located; searches and the Husch survey are silent. Not confirmed against a Wisconsin-specific retainage source.

retainageRelease.notes: No statutory deadline for private projects found.

payIfPaid.notes: Void: 'Provisions making a payment to a prime contractor from any person who does not have a contractual agreement with the subcontractor, supplier, or service provider a condition precedent to a prime contractor's payment'. Pay-when-paid (delay only) is expressly permitted.

lienWaiver.notes: No statutory form or notarization: any signed document purporting to waive lien rights is valid (§ 779.05(1)). NUANCE on advanceWaiverVoid: CONTRACT PROVISIONS requiring a lien claimant to waive lien/bond rights before being paid are void (§ 779.135(1)); but a separately signed waiver document is valid 'whether ... signed before or after' the work is performed, and unless expressly limited it waives ALL lien rights for work done or to be done (§ 779.05(1)). Claimant may refuse to give a waiver unless paid in full for the work it covers.

payIfPaid.cite: Wellington Power Corp. v. CNA Surety Corp., 217 W. Va. 33, 614 S.E.2d 680 (2005)
payIfPaid.notes: W. Va. Supreme Court upheld an explicit pay-if-paid condition precedent clause (public project / payment bond context; held not contrary to public policy of W. Va. Code § 38-2-39). Ziegenfuss Drilling v. Frontier-Kemper (S.D. W. Va. 2009) reads Wellington as upholding unambiguous pay-if-paid clauses generally. No private-project-specific appellate ruling found; reporter citation from memory/secondary sources, opinion itself not read.

payIfPaid.notes: No statute or Wyoming decision located; Husch Blackwell (2020): 'Wyoming has not yet addressed contingent payment clauses.'

lienWaiver.notes: § 29-10-101(b): the lien waiver 'shall be completed in substantially the following form'. Wyoming has ONE statutory form, not the four standard types: a waiver 'in consideration of the PAYMENT received to date' that reserves lien rights for retainage, and does not apply if the owner's payment is dishonored or revoked (closest analogue: progress waiver for payments received). The form includes a notary acknowledgment block, so notarizationRequired=true by inference from the form (the text does not separately say 'must be notarized'). Advance/contract waivers: secondary sources conflict (NCS says not waivable by contract; Levelset/Siteline/ezel say no express ban) -> null. Read on FindLaw copy, not wyoleg.gov.
